earlier_scan.note: Sign language; word stress inapplicable; Braithwaite refs are sociolinguistic/classificatory

sources.citation: Braithwaite, Ben. 2020. Emerging sign languages in the Caribbean. In Le Guen, Safar & Coppola (eds.), Emerging Sign Languages of the Americas, 251-286. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.note: The only published text treating SRSL (its section within the Caribbean survey); would confirm whether any structural remarks (lexicon, prosody) are made. Open access (CC BY-NC-ND) but the publisher PDF is behind a WAF challenge by automated download; a browser download would succeed.
sources.venue: Emerging Sign Languages of the Americas

sources.citation: Le Guen, Olivier, Marie Coppola & Josefina Safar. 2020. Introduction: How Emerging Sign Languages in the Americas contributes to the study of linguistics and (emerging) sign languages. In Le Guen, Safar & Coppola (eds.), Emerging Sign Languages of the Americas, 1-32. De Gruyter Mouton. doi:10.1515/9781501504884-001.
sources.note: Editors' summary of Braithwaite's chapter: SRSL is 'classified as a shared sign language, deaf people are integrated in the community'; deaf people 'more included into the wider society'. Nothing on phonology, prosody or stress.
sources.venue: Emerging Sign Languages of the Americas

sources.citation: Braithwaite, Ben, Lily Kwok & Rehana Omardeen. 2017. Documenting sign language in South Rupununi, Guyana. ICLDC 5 talk (audio recording).
sources.note: Audio of the talk is held by the project (braithwaite_kwok_omardeen2017_icldc_talk.mp3); a transcription would reveal what the 'initial sketch of some aspects of the structure' covered. No speech-to-text tool available by automated download.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'South Rupununi Sign Language' (stub); Wikidata Q85802311.
sources.note: Stub: used in at least seven Wapishana villages south of Lethem; sole reference is the 2017 ICLDC item. Nothing on structure.

sources.citation: Braithwaite, Ben. 2020. Ideologies of linguistic research on small sign languages in the global South: A Caribbean perspective. Language & Communication 74: 182-194.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Discusses the South Rupununi project as a case of research ideology; unlikely to contain structural description but is one of only a handful of texts naming the language.
